regions.name: feature_0
regions.why: sampled sub-grid feature cluster; no semantic part labels

regions.name: flow_lift_wake
regions.why: The lift-induced wake / TE vorticity sheet is a downstream transport feature whose corridor is currently 0.386% covered. A level-3 box (0.03125 m = half the declared 0.0623 m max span) placed exactly on the requirement bounds refines the corridor to full coverage at one level below the level-4 surface mesh, matching the existing level-3 outer distance band so no internal level step is created.

regions.name: flow_tip_left
regions.why: Left tip-vortex corridor is only 0.18% covered and its declared span (0.04981 m) is the tightest of the three; level 3 gives 0.03125 m, a factor 1.6 below the requirement, and overlaps the wake box so the union is one equal-level block along the vortex path (no transition defect inside the corridor).

regions.name: flow_tip_right
regions.why: Mirror tip-vortex corridor with identical 0.04981 m span requirement; level 3 = 0.03125 m meets it. Spanwise symmetry is preserved exactly (Y bounds mirrored about 0) so the two rolled-up vortices are resolved with equal nominal cell size, which matters because at AR~2 the two vortices interact.

advisor.hypothesis: The mesh is a first attempt with no native failure evidence; the one measured, deterministic defect is that the off-body requirements are effectively unrefined (configured coverage 0.00386 / 0.00182 / 0.00181). Cause: refinement is purely distance-driven around the body (bands 0.03125 m @ L4 and 0.09375 m @ L3) plus one level-6 near-trailing-edge feature box; nothing follows the flow downstream of X=0.996. The trailing-edge vorticity sheet and the two tip-vortex corridors are transport features, not proximity features, so they must be prescribed explicitly. Fixing this with three flow_refine boxes at level 3 (0.25/2^3 = 0.03125 m) satisfies both declared spans with margin (wake 0.03125 < 0.06226 m; tips 0.03125 < 0.04981 m), keeps the level jump to the level-4 surface mesh at exactly one level (n_cells_between_levels=3 inserts a buffer), and is consistent with the existing level-3 outer distance band so the union is a single level-3 block with no internal transition. Level 3 is the coarsest level that meets the strict max axis span; level 2 (0.0625 m) would exceed the tip span (0.0625 > 0.0498) and would only pass via the native p95 1.5x tolerance, and level 4 would cost ~680k extra cells and break the 2M gate. I deliberately do NOT touch layers, first height, n_grow or snap: there is no native extrusion/quality evidence yet, and the planning y+ estimate (h1 = 1.1087e-3 m, y+~50, stack 0.01829 m) is a surrogate, not a measurement.
advisor.expected_change: Scenario screen flips from accepted=false to accepted=true with configured volume coverage 0.00386/0.00182/0.00181 -> 1.0/1.0/1.0 for lift_wake/tip_left/tip_right, and nominal corridor cell size becomes 0.03125 m everywhere inside the corridors instead of 0.25 m background and 0.0625 m in the un-banded wake, downstream to X=2.9886 (3 chords past the trailing edge). Conservative cell forecast rises 1,693,778 -> 1,821,185 (91% of the 2,000,000 budget, +85k, i.e. less than the naive 8x-per-increment because the union of the three equal-level boxes is refined once). Uncertainty: the forecast is an unvalidated geometry upper bound and actual native cell count is a hard gate; the corridors themselves remain unvalidated hypotheses, so this intervention fixes resolution allocation, not vortex position or flow accuracy.
counterevidence: The corridors are unvalidated_physical_hypothesis: incidence/deflection may move the rolled-up tip vortex, so refining exactly the declared envelope could still miss the physical core - I keep the boxes matched to the requirement bounds instead of spending the remaining 9% budget on speculative enlargement.

Geometry measurements show p5 solid_normal_half_thickness 0.00845 m at thin TE/tip stations versus a requested layer stack of 0.01829 m and max_thickness_to_medial_ratio 0.3, and 33.4% of adjacent edges exceed the 60 deg layer feature angle, so extrusion may still trim or drop layers at the TE/tip - that is a separate mechanism with no native evidence yet.

unresolved_feature_fraction stays 0.0366 with and without the new boxes, confirming that off-body refinement does not address the unresolved sub-grid cluster and must not be sold as a geometry-fidelity fix.
Steady RANS mesh allocation cannot validate wake recovery or any unsteady shedding implied by the vorticity-sheet mechanism.
alternatives: Refine the same three corridors at level 4 (0.015625 m): passes spans with large margin but adds ~680k cells (conservative total ~2.37M) and would exceed max_global_cells, so it is not admissible now.
Refine the wake at level 2 (0.0625 m) to save ~43k cells: rejected because 0.0625 m exceeds the declared tip max span 0.04981 m and only the native p95 1.5x tolerance would mask it for the wake.

Widen refinement_bands (e.g. inner 0.03125 m @ L4, outer 0.15 m @ L3) to give the medial-axis shrinker more room around the thin TE/tip: deferred - it is cheap but unevidenced, and the thin-station half-thickness above suggests the shrinker, not the band depth, is the controlling risk.
Enlarge/shift the corridors beyond their declared bounds to hedge vortex drift: deferred until a flow solution exists, since it consumes the remaining budget margin with no measured trajectory.
